assertion.statement: The contact-prime selection in retained V13 completeness remains available after the roots, scales, bounded real neighborhoods and enlarged continuity modulus L have all been fixed.
assertion.objects: The prime family p_j and Gaussian generators pi_j; d_minus=N(pi_j-1), d_plus=N(pi_j+1).
assertion.hypotheses: All coefficients and arithmetic parameters are fixed before the prime limit; c_j are distinct after merging repeated forms. The earlier contact-form reduction and the identification of adjacent Gaussian norms with the two reduced group orders are retained separately.
assertion.quantifiers: Every fixed choice of those parameters; no uniform estimate over changing parameters.
assertion.parameter_range: k>=2,q>=1,M odd squarefree,7 not dividing M,H,Y>0.
assertion.uniformity: Existence for each fixed choice; all primes exceed the prescribed cutoff and the ratio exceeds the prescribed threshold.
assertion.constants: No effective or uniform bound for u,w is claimed.
assertion.normalizations: pi_j=9 mod16,1+3i mod7,i modM; v2(d_minus)=6,v2(d_plus)=2; cross-sign gcd4; adjacent norms are coprime to7M.
assertion.exceptional_cases: This use supplies the simultaneous primes and adjacent-norm data only. The separation lemma additionally needs the weighted Artin count, slow diagonal, strip removal and Hasse bound. Real density and CRT are separate retained arguments.
assertion.limit_order: Prepare roots, scales and continuity L first; apply the simultaneous-prime theorem with fixed data and sufficiently large cutoff. Then use the separate separation and real-progression arguments before choosing the final common index.

use.reason: The actual prime invocation occurs in the retained completeness chain at22583 and22715, not in the later coefficient-statistics paragraph. The chosen data precede the prime selection.
